observations.seen: Each venue has a different key, but none reads as an indoor flood rig at 55°/45°. Moon is a single hard light over a black void. Paris is monochrome orange with a hot spot near the net. Dubai is flat beige ambient with almost no modeling of form. Frame 1 has a soft central spotlight with a dark vignette and a green cast over the blue court.

Players and the umpire chair cast directional shadows. They are long and sharp in Moon and Paris, short and soft in Dubai. The net shadow is visible in Paris. There is little contact occlusion where the stands meet the floor, and the shadow edges in Moon look hard and slightly aliased.
No surface shows environment reflections or specular response. The court, stands, net posts and player kits all shade as matte diffuse, and the light poles look identical in every venue.

The stands, umpire chair, bench and signs sit on a bare floor plane. Beyond them is a void (Moon), a flat orange plane (Paris) or a beige plane (Dubai). Light poles have no fixtures. The Eiffel Tower is a blurred backdrop cut off by the frame top. There is no arena roof, walls or interior-industrial structure.
No indoor haze or light shafts are visible. Frame 1 has a greenish fog-like wash and a vignette. Paris has a faint warm gradient. Moon and Dubai have no atmosphere at all.

Court surfaces are flat single colors with a faint diagonal noise texture in frame 1. The service-box highlight is a flat pale-yellow quad. Crowd, stands and bench use untextured solid colors, and the clay court has no grain or scuffing.

Crowd members are repeated capsule figures in rainbow solids with identical poses. Players are low-poly, and the Moon variant swaps in white astronaut suits. The umpire chair and bench are simple boxes. The net is a thin line with visible kinks. Signage text is clipped to 'AURA SL M'.

In frames 2–4 the court fills about 30% of the frame, which is within target, but the upper third is wasted on empty floor and backdrop. In frame 1 the court fills about 70% of the frame and the HUD panels crowd the stands. The ball is barely visible in any frame.
Frames 2–4 use an elevated three-quarter broadcast view close to the recipe. Frame 1 switches to a much tighter, steeper perspective, so the shots are inconsistent.

Frame 1 has a heavy vignette and a green-teal color cast that muddies the blue court. Paris is crushed into a single orange hue. Dubai is low-contrast and washed out. There is no bloom on lights and no consistent arena grade.
Frame 1 has a clean scoreboard, power bar, ball-speed dial, mode pills and a controls strip, all readable. Frames 2–4 show only in-world signage with low-res pixel text and no overlay HUD.
